programmes.d: When Murray's wife ejects him from their home, Felix invites him to share his and Oscar's apartment.
Sportscaster Howard Cosell, in a neat bit of type-casting, plays Howard Cosell, a famous sportscaster who becomes involved in a feud with Oscar Madison.
Felix decides to become a writer and Oscar thinks he's wasting his time and money.
When Oscar's ulcer begins acting up, Felix decides an ocean voyage will do them both good.
Railroad President Norman Curtis thinks that his household's pet basset hound needs a change of scenery, so he sends the dog off to Shady Rest.
Kate Bradley is visited by an old schoolmate who's now a millionaire, but Uncle Joe has him pegged as a con artist.
Homer Bedloe returns to Hooterville with his son, Homer Junior, who is as hateful and devious as his father.
Business executive Mary Jane Hastings returns home to Hooterville and impresses everyone with her administrative ability, particularly her handling of men.
Laura gives Rob an expensive watch at his birthday party, but the watch goes missing.
Rob can't make up his mind when asked to be a candidate for the city council.
Rob agrees to run for office but realizes he'd prefer to vote for his brainy opponent.
Rob's parents gift a Petrie family heirloom to Laura, who accidentally drops it in the garbage disposal.
Carter and an old war buddy credit each other for being war heroes.
Duke talks Gomer into taking a jeep to the airport.
Gomer is a look-out for burglars robbing the base.
Gomer gets assigned to MP duty.
Carter wants his men to pass a promotion test.
Gomer holds a wedding ring for a friend and it appears to be lost when they spend a night baking bread.
The Germans have stolen a gold shipment from the French and Hogan must convince Klink to have it moved to the safety of Stalag 13.
While Hogan detains a German general during an Allied offensive, a Gestapo officer looks into Stalag 13's perfect escape record.
Hogan's latest underground contacts are secretly German spies.
Sergeant Schultz impersonates Klink in a scheme to get some of his men free from the Gestapo.
To get an Italian officer to defect, the Heroes use pizza to tempt him.
Hogan has a mission to move a mobile anti-aircraft artillery battery, but Klink's new tough second-in-command is impeding the Heroes.

Oliver's (Eddie Albert) nephew Charles (Don Edmonds) arrives for a visit, and Oliver is completely shaken up when the boy turns out to be a long-haired, motorcycle-ridin', hippy-dippy type. But, boy, does he know a thing or two about engines.

Oliver dreams of entering his crop in the Corn Festival, but the dreaded Bing Bug invades Hooterville's farms. After learning of his service as a WWII pilot, the locals volunteer him for the perilous task of flying the town's only crop duster.

When a lovely, young and successful farmer comes to Oliver (Eddie Albert) for his legal counsel, Lisa (Eva Gabor) quickly becomes jealous of the two spending time together and becomes determined to break up what she sees as a budding romance.

When the Monroe Brothers show up to fix the Douglas's closet, Lisa learns that Ralph is devastated because her true love has stood her up on another date. Lisa's solution: an intensive, two-day beauty treatment for Ralph…and the barn for Oliver!

Oliver (Eddie Albert) takes to his soap box, delivering fiery, patriotic speeches after getting a bill from the State Farm Unattached Duty Tax for an outrageous $12.03! But no one can figure out why the tax is levied in the first place.

Lisa (Eva Gabor) is curious to learn about the book that Oliver (Eddie Albert) is reading. It is the real-life story of pioneers Gus and Etta Thompson. The episode flashes back to the 19th century with Oliver appearing as Gus and Lisa as Etta.
Steve must take in a delinquent as a houseguest for a week.
Steve has to go to Japan for business and decides to bring the boys along.
Robbie and his friend Hank need money to go on dates, so they decide to start a business for home repairs and outdoor chores.

Tramp gets framed.

Mike and Lionel are planning on attending a demonstration at the United Nations. However, the rally gets out of hand and news of it appears on TV. This worries Gloria who begs Archie to go down there and get Mike.

A local election has the Bunker family in turmoil as Mike and Gloria are all for Claire Packer, a woman, which is why Archie is dead set against her. However, once down at the voting booths, Archie realizes that he can't vote because he isn't registered.

At the grocery store, Edith has an accident in the parking lot. She loses control of her shopping cart which smashes into a car and a can of Cling Peaches (in heavy syrup) flies out of the cart, onto the car, and makes a dent.

Mike is all stressed out with upcoming exams leaving him impotent and frustrated. Gloria encourages him to discuss it with her, but he refuses. Gloria confides in Edith what the problem is, and in turn she tells Archie.
Arthur instigates a doctors' strike, refusing to treat 'any' patients, but his convictions could prove to be very unhealthy when Walter and Vivian take ill.
Maude's up to her libido in sexual fantasies over a handsome government ecologist and Walter's up to his ears in jealousy.
The opening of a gay bar in the neighborhood sends a morally outraged Arthur to personally close its doors, while an infuriated Maude vows to dispel Arthur's bigotry.
More is at stake than the 'Businessman of the Year' award when Maude and Walter are the only two candidates.
'Twas the night before Christmas and all through the house...was chaos, Maude's holiday celebration seems to be turning out quite differently than she planned.
Maude's excitement over getting rid of an expensive white elephant turns to terror when she gets an offer she 'can't' refuse.
Joy blossoms at the Sunshine Cab Co. when a triumphant Bobby Wheeler returns to proclaim that he's landed a TV series role. Louie, in his own charming way, puts a damper on the celebration.
The pretty new cabbie proves to be more than Alex can handle when she leaves the meter running, in an attempt to lure him into romance.
A young runaway wreaks havoc at the Sunshine Cab Co. when Alex and Elaine encourage the lad to return home. Jim wants to adopt him, and Louie wants the youngster jailed for not paying his fare.

Romance and merriment are on the menu for Tony and Alex when they double-date gorgeous twin models at a posh restaurant, only to have the intimate group grow to a crowd with the unwelcome additions of Jim and Alex's ex-wife.
